text:
maria: quick question — contractor on the payments incident needs console access to inspect two erroring job traces and the billing view. Is org-level Viewer too broad or can we scope this to the project?
raj: scope to the project for sure. org-level is unnecessary. what exact resources do they need to see? logs? billing console? bigquery exports?
maria: logs in Cloud Logging for project redwood-pay-prod, and the billing console for that project only. also they might need to peek at a few BigQuery tables that contain delivery metadata (no PII).
raj: ok. propose: grant roles/logging.viewer + roles/bigquery.readSessionUser? maybe roles/bigquery.dataViewer on the specific dataset. and for billing, use Billing Account Viewer scoped via the project-billing binding if possible — but double-check billing account scope.
security-bot: :rotating_light: New access request created: AR-4831. Please include justification, expiration, and approver. See https://intranet/redwood/access-requests/AR-4831
maria: thanks. justification added: "investigate intermittent job failures affecting payment reconciliation". request expiry 48h. approver: @tanya.
tanya: I can approve for 48h if we use ephemeral creds and log all console sessions. we should also redact any raw card identifiers from logs before sharing.
raj: agreed on redaction. quick note on roles: roles/owner and roles/editor are definitely out. For least-priv, use these bindings at project redwood-pay-prod: 1) roles/logging.viewer 2) roles/bigquery.dataViewer (dataset-level) 3) roles/billing.viewer (if billing console needed, otherwise skip).
sam: small nit: billing.viewer is org/billing-scoped in GCP. if the billing account is shared, we might not be able to give project-level billing view. alternative: take a screenshot of the billing page and attach to the ticket (redacted) or create a temporary, limited billing report.
maria: thanks — can we do an ephemeral SA instead? create SA, grant the minimal roles, mint short-lived key via sts for 4h, then delete SA.
raj: yep, that's how I'd do it. steps (gcloud):
```
# create SA
gcloud iam service-accounts create incident-sleuth-4831 --project=redwood-pay-prod
# grant dataset viewer
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-pay-prod --member="serviceAccount:incident-sleuth-4831@redwood-pay-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/bigquery.dataViewer"
# mint short-lived creds with workload identity or sts
```
maria: pinging @tanya to approve AR-4831 so I can spin up the SA. also will attach the scrub script we use for logs.
tanya: approved for 48h. please follow the ephemeral SA flow and post the SA deletion step here when done. :white_check_mark:
raj: also ensure we update the access request with the dataset whitelist (payments_transfers, payment_audit). do not include any tables flagged PII.
maria: will do. scrub script (quick) to remove PANs from logs before sharing:
```
# simple sed redaction
sed -E 's/([0-9]{4}[- ]?){3}[0-9]{4}/[REDACTED_CARD]/g' export.log > export.redacted.log
```
security-bot: Reminder: all console sessions for AR-4831 will be recorded and stored in audit-logs/requests/AR-4831 for 90 days.
sam: FYI if you hit permission denied on bigquery read, check dataset IAM or authorized views. sometimes we bind to the project but dataset policy is tighter.
maria: noted. I'll update AR-4831 with dataset names and the scrub confirmation, then create the SA. I'll post the deletion timestamp when done. thanks all. :bow:)
